panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is an OCT cross-section showing drusen-like lesions, a documented ophthalmic manifestation associated with Macular Dystrophy in SPG11, based on the article title and caption. B: Panel B shows a hyperautofluorescent lesion in the macular region, which is part of the documented ophthalmic presentation of SPG11. C: Panel C shows an OCT of a hypoautofluorescent lesion associated with the same maculopathy being studied in the context of SPG11.
panels.attribution_text: Grech et al. Macular Dystrophy Associated With Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia Type 11 (Kjellin Syndrome): A Multidisciplinary Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106325. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Section through the drusen-like lesions (marked by red asterisk) showed small-medium sized, moderately reflective mounds in the photoreceptor layer with disruption of the interdigitation zone and variable attenuation and upwards deviation of the ellipsoid zone, with protrusion towards and inner deviation of the external limiting membrane. The lesions were in different stages of severity (B) A section through a hyperautofluorescent lesion revealed the drusen-like lesion (marked by red asterisk) (C) A section through a hypoautofluorescent lesion was unremarkable (marked by red asterisk)
in_text_mentions: The OCT appearance of the macular drusen-like lesions varied according to their autofluorescence (Figures 3, 4). This implies that lesions evolve over time with eventual resorption, and new lesions (likely hyperautofluorescent) coexisting with older ones (likely hypoautofluorescent). Blue autofluorescence photos of the posterior poles revealed a reticular pattern of discrete amoeboid hyperautofluorescent lesions with a thick hypofluorescent rim. Some lesions, especially those close to the main arcades, were mostly hypoautofluorescent.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A provides OCT findings (left side) and corresponding fundus image (right side) of the right macula, showing specific manifestations (photoreceptor hyperreflectivity, disruption of the interdigitation zone, increased signal transmission) in the context of SPG11-related macular dystrophy. B: Panel B provides OCT findings (left side) and corresponding fundus image (right side) of the left macula, showing bilateral retinal pathology including disruption of the interdigitation zone and increased signal transmission.
panels.attribution_text: Grech et al. Macular Dystrophy Associated With Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia Type 11 (Kjellin Syndrome): A Multidisciplinary Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106325. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Macular OCT using Topcon DRI OCT Triton (red asterisk: The right fovea showed localized photoreceptor hyperreflectivity, and there was bilateral disruption of the interdigitation zone and increased signal transmission; A: right macula OCT; B: left macula OCT) OCT: Optical coherence tomography
in_text_mentions: Humphrey central automated perimetry was normal on the right, but showed a mild superior extension of the left blind spot. Goldmann kinetic perimetry was normal. Optical coherence tomography (OCT), done in March 2025, revealed that the right fovea showed localized photoreceptor hyperreflectivity, and there was bilateral disruption of the interdigitation zone and increased signal transmission (Figure 2). Increased signal transmission indicates retinal pigment epithelial attenuation.

in_text_mentions: The OCT appearance of the macular drusen-like lesions varied according to their autofluorescence (Figures 3, 4). This implies that lesions evolve over time with eventual resorption, and new lesions (likely hyperautofluorescent) coexisting with older ones (likely hypoautofluorescent). Blue autofluorescence photos of the posterior poles revealed a reticular pattern of discrete amoeboid hyperautofluorescent lesions with a thick hypofluorescent rim. Some lesions, especially those close to the main arcades, were mostly hypoautofluorescent.
